home.title: Gradient: the Shades Media Group design system
home.description: Gradient is the design system of Shades Media Group: the logo, colour, type, the Spectra characters, components and icons every Shades product is built from. Open source.

hero.title: Every Shades product starts here.
hero.lead: Gradient is how Shades Media Group looks, speaks and builds: one mark, one red, seven characters, and the code every project installs.
hero.note: Free and open source. The name and the mark stay ours.

split.label: The three bars of the mark

brand.title: Brand
brand.text: The mark, the lockup, the Spectra family and the way Shades writes.

foundations.title: Foundations
foundations.text: Colour, type, space and motion, each defined once and used everywhere.

code.title: Code
code.text: CSS components, a Tailwind theme and 78 Shades icons in one package.

split.caption: Three bars at full, 75% and 50% white. That is the whole idea: shades of one colour, side by side, make a gradient.

colour.title: One red. Used like a signal.
colour.text: Shades Red, #E40523, is the red of the mark itself. It marks the one action that matters on a screen and may fill one chapter of a page. Everything else is ink and paper.
colour.red: The Shades Red scale, from 50 to 900
colour.ink: The ink scale, from paper to ink
colour.rule: Red is the signal, never the wallpaper. The four-shade spectrum appears once per layout, as a strip.

type.title: Space Grotesk speaks. Hanken Grotesk explains.
type.text: Headlines are set heavy and tight in Space Grotesk. Everything you read at length is Hanken Grotesk. Russian falls back to Inter and Chinese to the system face, so every language reads as cleanly as English.
type.body: Body text is set at 17 pixels with room to breathe, and numbers line up because they use tabular figures, not a typewriter face.

family.title: Seven shades, one family.
family.text: Spectra walked out of the logo, crest and all. Six coworkers followed, each with one job: Sage explains, Nova announces, Sunny confirms that it shipped.

parts.title: The parts, working.
parts.text: Every component is a plain class that reads the tokens. It works in React, Preact or plain HTML, and a client brand can recolour the whole set by changing a few variables.
parts.name: Your name
parts.emailError: Add the part after the @, like ana@company.md.
parts.demo: A demo built from Gradient parts. It sends nothing.
parts.sent: Checked and ready. This demo stops here.

licence.title: Open code. Our name.
licence.text: The tokens, styles and icons are MIT: use them in anything. The Shades name, the mark and the Spectra characters belong to Shades Media Group and its own work.

work.title: Built from real work.
work.text: Every rule here came from a product Shades shipped, including the parts we threw away.
work.pagerecast: Turns any web page into editable Figma layers. It taught us what reads as made by hand and what reads as generated.
work.nails: A booking app for a nail studio. It proved a client brand can wear the same parts in its own colours.
work.lms: Our own life-management app. It set the rules for icons and motion on a phone.
work.imagereframe: Free, open image export and import for Figma. The first product to start from Gradient.
work.shades: The agency's own site, to be rebuilt on Gradient.

install.title: Three ways in.
install.text: One package, shades-gradient, for every Shades project. Pick the part your stack needs.
install.anyText: Tokens, base styles, components and motion in one stylesheet, about 6 KB compressed.
install.tailwindText: Every token becomes a utility that follows light and dark: bg-accent, text-text-2, rounded-pill.
install.iconsText: 78 Shades icons as SVG strings, or one sprite for plain HTML.
install.preferred: Find Gradient more often in Google Search:

what.a: Gradient is the design system of Shades Media Group: brand rules, design tokens, CSS components, icons and the Spectra characters. The code ships as the shades-gradient npm package, and this site documents it.

use.q: Can I use Gradient in my own project?
use.a: Yes. The code is MIT, so you can use the tokens, components and icons in anything. The Shades name, the mark and the Spectra characters are not covered by that licence and stay with Shades Media Group.

stack.q: Does Gradient need React or Tailwind?
stack.a: No. Components are plain CSS classes and icons are SVG strings, so they work with any framework or none. Tailwind v4 projects can import a theme that turns every token into utilities.

client.q: How does a client brand use it?
client.a: Override the role tokens, such as --g-accent, --g-bg and --g-text, in one stylesheet. Components read only those, so the whole set takes the client's colours at once.

red.a: It is the red of the Shades logo file on shades.md, which is the brand's source of truth. Earlier explorations used other reds; Gradient keeps one.

brand.title: Brand: the Shades mark, the Spectra family and voice | Gradient
brand.description: The Shades logo and how to use it, the seven Spectra characters and their jobs, and how Shades Media Group writes.
brand.heading: The brand
brand.lead: One mark, seven characters and a way of writing. Everything here is drawn from the files Shades already ships.

logo.title: The mark
logo.text: A sharp red square holding three white bars at full, 75% and 50%. The bars are the shades in the name. It is never redrawn: every file comes from the same geometry on shades.md.
logo.reverseAlt: The Shades lockup in white beside the red mark, on ink.
logo.anatomyAlt: The mark on its construction grid: one bar width of clear space on every side.
logo.fieldText: Shades Red #E40523, a square with sharp corners.
logo.barsText: Three bars, each one tenth of the square wide and more than half its height, white at 100%, 75% and 50%.
logo.spaceText: One bar width on every side. Nothing else enters it.
logo.sizeText: 16 px on screen as a favicon, 24 px in an interface, 8 mm in print.
logo.misuseRound: Round the corners. The mark is square.
logo.misuseTint: Tint the bars pink or rose. They are white.
logo.misuseStretch: Stretch it or change its proportions.
logo.misuseGradient: Fill it with the spectrum or any gradient.

family.title: The Spectra family
family.text: Seven characters, one per kind of moment. They share the same eyes, the three-bar crest from the mark and a quiet smile, and each has one flat colour.

spectra.text: Walked out of the logo the day it was finished. Opens decks, greets new users and fronts launches.
spectra.where: Home pages, onboarding, launch decks, the first slide

mera.text: Measured and precise. Appears next to plans, timelines and anything that needs a decision.

sol.text: The loud one, with one arm always up. Used for creative work, reviews and inspiration.

nova.text: The smallest, with a spark overhead. Announces betas and new features.

sage.text: Patient and kind, eyes closed while listening. Owns tutorials, tooltips and the help centre.

vio.text: Witty and warm, always mid-wink. Speaks on social, in campaigns and to the community.

sunny.text: Steady and practical. Confirms progress, success and delivery.

family.rule1: Same eyes on everyone: a white disc, a black pupil and one highlight.
family.rule2: The three-bar crest is never removed. It is the family name.
family.rule3: One soft shape per body, every corner rounded.
family.rule4: One quiet curved smile. No teeth, no open grin.
family.rule5: They hover over a soft shadow. They never stand.
family.rule6: One flat colour each. No gradients on bodies.
family.motion: One character per moment and at most two on a screen. Never in the logo's place. Their idle loops stop when the reader asks for reduced motion.
family.never1: Recolour a character or swap two silhouettes.
family.never2: Add teeth, an open grin or a new expression outside the set.
family.never3: Put a character in the logo’s place or beside it as a second logo.
family.never4: Show one smaller than 48 px on screen or 15 mm in print.

voice.title: How Shades writes
voice.text: Short, confident, specific. We sell the result, not the feature, and every piece ends with one clear next step.
voice.sloganRule: The main line. One slogan per surface, never stacked with others.
voice.noExample: We are a creative powerhouse where design, marketing and technology converge to deliver unique solutions.
voice.yesExample: We build brands people recognise and sites that bring them work. Start with a brief.
voice.rule2: Lead with the outcome, then how.
voice.rule3: Short declarative lines. One idea each.
voice.rule4: Show real results or say nothing. Never invent numbers, quotes or clients.
voice.rule5: No emoji in brand copy. Icons and the mark do that work.
voice.tagsText: What a project is, said as a tag with a red #. Three at most, never as decoration.

lockups.title: Lockups and placement
lockups.text: Four arrangements cover every use. Each comes from the same geometry and ships as a file.
lockups.horizontalText: The mark and SHADES side by side. The default for sites, documents and footers.
lockups.markText: Where there is room for one square: favicons, app icons, avatars and anything under 120 px wide.
lockups.reverseText: The wordmark in white for ink, dark photographs and the dark theme. The mark stays red.
lockups.monoText: Bars cut out of the square for foil, embroidery, etching, stamps and single-colour print.
lockups.place1: In interfaces the logo sits top left and links home. It is never centred in a navigation bar.
lockups.place2: On print covers and merchandise it sits top left or dead centre, never in a corner at an angle.
lockups.place3: Keep one bar width of clear space on every side, more where the layout allows.
lockups.place4: Never place it over busy imagery. Use a solid red, ink or paper ground behind it.

sizes.title: Sizes
sizes.text: The mark stays crisp from a 16 px favicon to a building sign. Below each minimum, use the mark alone.

colourUse.title: Colour in use
colourUse.text: The proportions that make a layout read as Shades at a glance. Paper and ink carry the page; red is the signal.
colourUse.shareLabel: Paper 60 per cent, ink 25, red 12, spectrum 3
colourUse.shareNote: A rough share of a typical page or poster. The spectrum is the last sliver, once.
colourUse.rule1: Body text is ink or white. Red text is for links and one highlighted word, never a paragraph.
colourUse.rule2: Ink on red and white on the spectrum colours pass only at 24 px and up, or 19 px bold.
colourUse.rule3: The four spectrum shades appear together, in order, as one strip. Never one alone as a background.
colourUse.rule4: Client brands bring their own accent. Shades Red never appears in a client product.

type.title: Type in the brand
type.text: Two families, each with one job. The wordmark is drawn, not typed.
type.display: Display: headlines, numbers that lead, the lockup. Weights 500 to 700, tight tracking.
type.body: Text: everything read at length, interfaces, captions. Weights 400 to 700, normal tracking.
type.rule1: Headlines in sentence case. Only the wordmark is set in capitals.
type.rule2: Two weights per layout are enough; three is the most.
type.rule3: Never set the word SHADES in a font to stand in for the logo. Use the file.
type.rule4: Numbers that are compared line up: tabular figures in the text face.
type.rule5: Romanian uses ș and ț with a comma below, never ş and ţ with a cedilla.

imagery.title: Photography and imagery
imagery.text: Images show real work and real people. The brand supplies the colour; the photograph supplies the truth.
imagery.yes1: Real projects, real screens, real teams at work
imagery.yes2: Natural light from one side, honest colour
imagery.yes3: Tight crops with room in the direction of the gaze
imagery.yes4: One strong image rather than five weak ones
imagery.no1: Stock renders, AI-generated scenes, glossy 3D blobs
imagery.no2: Text or gradients baked into the photograph
imagery.no3: Filters that push the image towards red to match the brand
imagery.no4: Images that decorate and explain nothing
imagery.alt: Alt text is written like a caption: what the picture shows and why it is there.

moments.title: Writing by moment
moments.text: The same voice, adjusted to what the reader is going through.
moments.errorRule: Say what happened and how to fix it. No blame, no codes.
moments.errorExample: That email is missing the part after the @.
moments.successRule: Confirm in one line and say what happens next.
moments.successExample: Sent. We reply within one working day.
moments.emptyRule: Say what will be here and offer the first step.
moments.emptyExample: No projects yet. Start one with a brief.
moments.buttonRule: A verb and its object, two to four words.
moments.marketingRule: Lead with the result, then the proof, then one action.
moments.marketingExample: Brands people recognise, sites that bring them work.
moments.mech1: Sentence case for headings, buttons and labels.
moments.mech2: Numbers as digits; units with a space: 24 px, 10 minutes.
moments.mech3: Dates written out in the reader’s language: 4 March 2027, 4 martie 2027.
moments.mech4: Times in 24 hours in Romanian and Russian, as the reader’s locale prefers elsewhere.
moments.mech5: No exclamation marks in interfaces. One per campaign, if earned.

products.title: Products and sub-brands
products.text: Which mark each product wears, and how it credits Shades.
products.name: Name
products.gradientMark: The Shades mark beside the word Gradient
products.pagerecastMark: Its own mark: two overlapping pages
products.imagereframeMark: Its own mark, to be drawn
products.clientMark: The client’s own brand, on Gradient roles
products.note: A product may have its own mark. It still uses Gradient’s type, roles, icons and rules, and its credit line never changes.

foundations.title: Foundations: colour, type, space and motion | Gradient
foundations.description: The Gradient design tokens: Shades Red and the ink scale, semantic roles for light and dark, the type scale, spacing, radius and motion.
foundations.heading: Foundations
foundations.lead: Every value is written once, in tokens.json, and reaches CSS, Tailwind and JSON from there. Click any swatch to copy its variable.

colour.title: Colour
colour.text: Shades Red and a neutral ink scale do almost all the work. The four spectrum shades exist for one strip per layout.
colour.spectrumRule: Blue, magenta, red and orange, in that order. Once per layout, as a strip or a rule, never as a background or on text.
colour.copy: Click a swatch to copy its custom property.

roles.title: Roles
roles.text3: Hints and captions, the quietest readable text
roles.accent: The one primary action and selection
roles.accentText: Red text on light or dark ground
roles.theming: A client brand changes the roles in one stylesheet. Every component follows, because none of them reads a raw colour.

type.title: Type
type.text: Space Grotesk for display and headings, Hanken Grotesk for everything else. Sizes above the body scale with the screen.
type.bodySample: Shades builds brands and the products around them, from the first sketch to the shipped site.
type.rule1: Tracking tightens as size grows, down to -0.04em at display size. Body text is never tracked.
type.rule2: Numbers use tabular figures in the body face. Monospace is only for code someone types.
type.rule3: No small capitals or tracked labels above headings. The heading carries its own weight.
type.rule4: Buttons and links are never italic.

space.title: Space and shape
space.text: A 4 px base in ten steps. More space above a heading than below it, tight inside groups and generous between them.

motion.title: Motion
motion.text: Three speeds for the interface and one for the characters. Content is visible before anything moves.
motion.move: Things that travel: panels, reveals, the house curve.
motion.loop: Spectra idles and the loader only.
motion.reduced: Under prefers-reduced-motion every animation stops and every transition is instant. Nothing important depends on motion.

elevation.title: Elevation
elevation.text: Three neutral shadows lift things off the page. The red one sits only under the one primary action.
elevation.sm: Controls on a surface, the raised segment
elevation.md: Panels, menus and the brief form
elevation.lg: Dialogs, popovers and the display panel
elevation.accent: The primary button, light theme only
elevation.rule: Shadows always have an offset and a soft blur. No glows, no coloured halos on dark grounds.

layout.title: Layout
layout.text: One column on phones, two from tablets up, all inside a 1240 px measure.
layout.name: Range
layout.phoneWhat: One column, full-width buttons, the mark splits without pinning
layout.largeWhat: Two-column grids return for small items
layout.tabletWhat: Chapter heads and documents become two columns
layout.desktopWhat: The full navigation, pinned scenes, side-by-side specimens
layout.rule: Layouts reflow; they never scale down. Text stays readable without zooming at every width.

contrast.title: Contrast
contrast.text: Every text role against the background it sits on, measured from the tokens at build time.
contrast.note: AA needs 4.5 : 1 for body text, AAA 7 : 1. The build fails if any of these drops below AA.

components.title: Components: buttons, fields, choices and labels | Gradient
components.description: Live Gradient components with their states and the HTML to copy: buttons, fields, switches, segmented controls, tags, badges, disclosure and the brand parts.
components.heading: Components
components.lead: Plain classes that read the tokens. Copy the HTML, add the stylesheet, and they work in any framework.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.text: Pills, because the mark is square and actions should not be. One red primary per view.
buttons.rule1: Label the action with a verb: Send, Save, Start. Never OK or Submit.
buttons.rule2: While busy, the label keeps its width and the three bars take its place.
buttons.rule3: An icon-only button always has an aria-label.
buttons.useLg: The one call to action on a page

fields.title: Fields
fields.text: A visible label above every field, a hint when it helps, and an error that says how to fix it.
fields.name: Full name
fields.nameHint: As it should appear on the contract.
fields.briefPlaceholder: What should change after the work is done?

choices.title: Choices
choices.text: A segmented control switches between views of the same thing. A switch applies at once; a checkbox waits for a submit.

labels.title: Tags and badges
labels.text: A hashtag says what something is. A badge says what state it is in.

disclosure.title: Disclosure and tables
disclosure.text: Answers open in place, without script. Tables line their numbers up and use hairlines, not boxes.
disclosure.a1: When the brief is signed and the first payment arrives. We send the plan within a week.
disclosure.a2: You do, once the project is paid. We keep the right to show it in our portfolio unless you ask us not to.

brand.title: Brand parts
brand.text: The pieces only Shades has: the mark that animates its bars, the loader made of those bars, and the spectrum strip.
brand.rule: The spectrum strip appears once per layout. The animated mark is for loading screens and the moment a page first opens, not for navigation.

navigation.title: Navigation
navigation.text: Tabs switch between views of one thing. Breadcrumbs say where a page sits.
navigation.rule1: Use tabs for views of the same object, never as a second navigation bar.
navigation.rule2: The current tab is marked with a red line and aria-selected; arrow keys move between tabs.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.text: Messages explain, progress reassures, toasts confirm. None of them shouts.
feedback.successText: We reply within one working day.
feedback.warningText: Save your changes to keep them.
feedback.dangerText: It is larger than 25 MB. Compress it and try again.
feedback.rule1: A message names the problem and the way out, in that order.
feedback.rule2: Errors use role="alert"; confirmations use role="status" so screen readers hear them once.
feedback.rule3: A toast lasts about two seconds and never holds an action someone must take.

people.title: People
people.text: Avatars show who is behind a project: a photo when there is one, initials on a family colour when there is not.
people.rule: Initials are two letters, first and last name. Colours come from the Spectra family, never from the accent.

access.title: Accessibility
access.text: Every component works with a keyboard and a screen reader before it ships.
access.btnKeys: Tab to reach, Enter or Space to press
access.btnReader: Its label; aria-busy while it works
access.fieldKeys: Tab between fields; errors move focus to the first problem
access.fieldReader: Label, hint and error read in order through aria-describedby
access.choiceKeys: Arrow keys inside a group, Space to toggle a switch
access.choiceReader: Role radio or switch, with its checked state
access.navKeys: Arrow keys between tabs, Home and End to the ends
access.navReader: Tablist and tab roles; the breadcrumb marks the current page
access.feedbackReader: Status and alert roles, read once without moving focus
access.note: Focus is always visible: a two-pixel red ring with a gap, in both themes.

icons.title: Icons: the Shades icon set | Gradient
icons.description: 78 Shades interface icons drawn on a 24 px grid with 2 px round strokes, free to use under MIT, plus the marks of the services Shades links to.
icons.heading: Icons
icons.lead: Shades' own set, drawn for Gradient: 24 px grid, 2 px round strokes, one file per icon. Click an icon to copy its name.
icons.empty: No icon by that name yet. Draw it to the rules below and add it.

set.title: The set
set.text: Interface icons in currentColor, so they take the colour of the text around them.

rules.title: Drawing rules
rules.text: Every icon follows the same five rules, so a new one sits with the rest.
rules.rule1: 24 × 24 grid with 2 px of padding: drawing stays between 2 and 22.
rules.rule2: 2 px strokes with round caps and joins. Fill only for dots of 1 to 1.6 px.
rules.rule3: Corners of 2 px on rectangles. No sharp boxes, no thin hairlines.
rules.rule4: currentColor only. Never a fixed colour inside the file.
rules.rule5: An icon must mean something. If the label alone is clear, leave the icon out.

marks.title: Other services
marks.text: Filled marks of the services Shades links to, from Simple Icons. They belong to their owners: use them only to link to those services.

print.title: Print: cards, badges, merchandise and email | Gradient
print.description: Shades print and merchandise rules: business card, event badge, tote, tee, stickers, the email signature and colour for print.
print.heading: Print and merchandise
print.lead: The same mark and the same restraint on paper, cloth and email. Sizes are real; the colour values still need a printer's proof.

card.title: Business card
card.text: The front is only the mark on red. The back carries the person, set in the brand type on paper.
card.front: Front: the mark, centred, on Shades Red
card.back: Back: name, role and contacts on paper
card.sample: Sample person and details. The card is drawn at its real proportions.

badge.title: Event badge
badge.text: First names large, enough to read across a room. The colour band says who someone is.
badge.holeText: One slot, centred, 10 mm from the top
badge.name: Name
badge.nameText: First name in Space Grotesk, at least 18 mm tall

merch.title: Merchandise
merch.text: Small mark or big wordmark, never both on one item. The spectrum only as a trim.
merch.toteText: One-colour mark, screen printed, on natural canvas.
merch.teeText: The wordmark large across the back, the chest left empty.
merch.stickerText: A Spectra character, die cut with a 3 mm white border.
merch.rule1: Use the one-colour files for embroidery, foil, etching and screen print.
merch.rule2: Never print the mark smaller than 8 mm.
merch.rule3: One character per item. The characters never replace the mark.

signature.title: Email signature
signature.text: Five lines at most, live text rather than one big image, so it reads with images turned off.
signature.rule1: The mark at 48 px, linked to shades.md.
signature.rule2: Name, role, then one line of contacts. No slogans, no banners.

colour.title: Colour for print
colour.text: Screens use the hex values. Print needs a spot or process match checked against a real proof.
colour.redPrint: Match to a warm spot red on a printed proof before the first run
colour.inkPrint: Rich black: C60 M40 Y40 K100 on coated stock
colour.paperPrint: The paper itself; never print a tint for white
colour.proof: No print value is final until a printer has proofed it. Record the approved values here, with the printer and the stock.

projects.title: Projects: how Shades products were made | Gradient
projects.description: How PageRecast was built, what the team kept and threw away, the lessons every Shades project now follows, and what comes next.
projects.heading: Built from real work
projects.lead: Gradient keeps the decisions behind each product: what we made, what the owner rejected, and the rule it left behind.

pagerecast.text: A free Chrome extension and Figma plugin that turn any web page into editable layers. Built in October 2026, published on the Chrome Web Store, the Figma Community and npm.
pagerecast.s1Text: The first version was thrown out completely. The rebuild began with a plan of every feature people expected and a few the market was asking for.
pagerecast.s2Text: Over twenty logo directions. The shadowed and three-dimensional ones went; a flat overlap of two pages stayed, the way Google and Apple marks work.
pagerecast.s3Text: Round after round, the owner pointed at parts that felt made by a template. Each one became a rule.
pagerecast.s4Text: Chrome Web Store, Figma Community, npm, a site on Cloudflare Workers, releases and a wiki.
pagerecast.s5Text: The extension, the plugin and the site in English, French, Romanian, Russian, Spanish and Chinese, with search markup on every page.
pagerecast.kept1: Pill buttons with a clear arrow, and the old buttons where people liked them
pagerecast.kept2: The real product shown working, never a drawing of it
pagerecast.kept3: Bold full-width chapters, one of them red
pagerecast.kept4: The company credit only in the product, the founder's in the README
pagerecast.cut2: Fake browser windows and grey skeleton drawings
pagerecast.cut3: Icons on every row and lists in rounded boxes
pagerecast.cut4: The same red block reused in every section

lessons.title: Lessons every project follows
lessons.text: These come from the owner's own corrections. A Shades product breaks none of them.
lessons.link: The full list in the repository
lessons.l1Text: The actual product, page or capture. If it does not exist yet, show nothing rather than a mock.
lessons.l2Text: Numbers use tabular figures in the body face. Monospace is for code only.
lessons.l3Text: No small tracked words, no section numbers. The heading speaks for itself.
lessons.l4: Icons only when they mean something
lessons.l4Text: No icon on every row, no icon in a circle as the centre of an empty state.
lessons.l5Text: Lists sit on hairlines. Cards are rare and never nested.
lessons.l6Text: Logos are flat and two-dimensional. No shadows, no glossy app-icon renders.
lessons.l7Text: Dense and purposeful, never empty for effect and never crowded with filler.
lessons.l8Text: Static HTML, no third-party scripts, self-hosted fonts. A Shades page opens instantly on a phone.

next.title: Next on Gradient
next.text: The products that will start from this system instead of from a template.
next.imagereframe: Image export and import for Figma, free and open source, built under the Shades brand with features the market is missing.
next.shades: The agency site, rebuilt: keep its best ideas, drop the template look.

start.title: Start a new project
start.text: The same five steps every time, so the next product starts where the last one finished.
start.s1Text: Who it is for, what it does, what it must never do. PRODUCT.md in the repository root.
start.s2Text: npm i shades-gradient, then import the stylesheet or the Tailwind theme.
start.s3: Decide its own mark, or wear the Shades one
start.s3Text: A product can have its own logo, but it uses Gradient's type, roles and rules.
start.s4Text: Before the first screen, not after the fifth review.
start.s5Text: Typecheck, tests, the site audit and screenshots in light and dark before anything is called done.

consent.title: Your privacy
consent.text: This site keeps only what it needs to work, like your display settings. Analytics or marketing tools would run only with your yes.
consent.necessaryText: Remembers your display and privacy choices. Always on.
consent.analyticsText: Anonymous visit counts, to learn what helps. Not in use on this site today.
consent.marketingText: Ads and campaign measurement. Not in use on this site today.

email.title: Email: Outlook-safe templates with calendar invites | Gradient
email.description: Transactional email in the Shades system that works in Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail, with copyable codes, calendar invites and Gmail markup.
email.heading: Email
email.lead: Transactional email that holds up in every inbox, Outlook on Windows included, with codes people can copy and invites that land in their calendar.

previews.title: Previews
previews.text: Three real emails, rendered by the package at build time.
previews.note: Sample people and details. The emails are shown in English; they take any language.

clients.title: What works where
clients.text: Tested features per client. Where a client cannot do something, the email still reads correctly.
clients.note: Outlook on Windows draws email with Microsoft Word, so buttons are VML shapes and every font falls back to Arial there.

codes.title: Codes people can copy
codes.text: Gmail offers a Copy button and Apple Mail offers AutoFill when a code is written the right way.
codes.rule1: Put the word “code” and the digits next to each other, as plain text, never in an image.
codes.rule2: Keep the digits in one run: no spaces, dashes or separate table cells.
codes.rule3: Repeat the code in the subject: “Your Shades code: 418203”.
codes.rule4: Say how long it works and what to do if the reader did not ask for it.

calendar.title: Calendar invites
calendar.text: Bookings arrive as an invitation, so the time lands in the reader’s calendar in one tap.
calendar.rule1: Attach an .ics invite with an organiser and an attendee: Gmail and Outlook show it as an event card with Yes, No and Maybe.
calendar.rule2: Keep the same UID for the same booking and raise SEQUENCE on every change, so a new time replaces the old one.
calendar.rule3: Send METHOD:CANCEL with the same UID to remove a cancelled booking from the calendar.
calendar.rule4: Add Google Calendar and Outlook links under the booking for readers who prefer a link.

build.title: Build one
build.text: Blocks in, HTML and plain text out. Every value is escaped and only http(s) links get through.
build.rule1: One heading, one lead, one primary button. The rest is detail.
build.rule2: Always send the plain-text part; some readers and filters only see that.
build.rule3: Gmail markup shows only for senders registered with Google that pass SPF and DKIM. It is safe to include either way.
build.rule4: Client brands pass their own colours, logo and font in brand; the structure stays the same.
